summary: This episode tells of the request of the twelve Yathrib youths after the first Pledge of Aqabah that the Prophet ﷺ send a teacher to teach the Quran and lead prayer, and he sent Mus'ab ibn Umair and later Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum. The ustaz explains why they were chosen, the six traits of a da'i, the story of Mus'ab who was martyred at Uhud without enough shroud, and of Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum who was the reason Surah Abasa was revealed. He tells how As'ad ibn Zurarah mapped Yathrib for Mus'ab, how Usayd and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh, who came angry, accepted Islam after hearing the Quran, how the whole of Banu Abd al-Ashhal believed except Usayrim, who accepted Islam on the day of Uhud, and how As'ad began the first Friday gathering before the Hijra. The ustaz ties it all to building a community on the Quran, avoiding two extremes in tadabbur, and guarding sincerity against the disease of popularity.
keyPoints: Twelve Yathrib youths asked for a teacher to teach the Quran and lead prayer, the two most basic things that our own families need too.
The Prophet ﷺ chose Mus'ab ibn Umair, young, tested in sacrifice and a master of the Quran, with the more senior Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum as balance.
Six traits of a da'i: mastery of the Quran, skill with people, good character, wisdom, strong faith and zeal to spread it.
As'ad ibn Zurarah, a local, mapped Yathrib for Mus'ab, and they worked systematically, not haphazardly.
Usayd and Sa'd ibn Mu'adh came angry but accepted Islam after Mus'ab offered them a hearing first and recited Surah Az-Zukhruf.
The whole of Banu Abd al-Ashhal believed through Mus'ab except Usayrim, who accepted Islam on the morning of Uhud and was martyred before he could pray.
Tadabbur of the Quran needs scholarly discipline but must not be made frightening, and the greatest test of a da'i is the love of popularity.

lessons.title: Two most basic things: Quran and prayer
lessons.body: The request for a teacher was to teach the Quran and lead prayer, and those are also the two foundations in our families.

lessons.title: Choose da'is with the right traits
lessons.body: A degree is not enough; mastery of the Quran, interpersonal skill, character, wisdom, tested faith and zeal to spread it are needed.

lessons.title: Da'wah work does not always show results
lessons.body: Mus'ab built Madinah but did not live to enjoy the result; sincere effort cannot depend on seeing outcomes.

lessons.title: Accept correction without defending yourself
lessons.body: The Prophet ﷺ accepted Allah's correction about Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum without justification and honoured that Companion all his life.

lessons.title: Balance young zeal with senior maturity
lessons.body: The Prophet sent the young Mus'ab with the more senior Abdullah so the foundation was built in balance.

lessons.title: Work systematically
lessons.body: A da'i cannot be careless; Mus'ab and As'ad had phases and mapped the clans before approaching them.

lessons.title: Offer a hearing first, with confidence
lessons.body: Mus'ab asked to be heard first and promised to leave if they disliked it, an attitude that opens the heart of those who come angry.

lessons.title: Sincerity from the start
lessons.body: As'ad reminded Mus'ab to be sincere even as a good opportunity opened up, because da'wah begins with sincerity.

lessons.title: Build community with shared routines
lessons.body: Friday gatherings, congregational prayer and shared classes became the pulse of a community that united the Aws and Khazraj.

lessons.title: Avoid two extremes in Quran tadabbur
lessons.body: Keep the discipline of tafsir but do not scare people away from learning the Quran, because the Quran is the same for everyone.

lessons.title: Train leaders and give trust
lessons.body: The Prophet appointed new leaders and trusted Mus'ab; a community dies when leaders do not make room for others.

lessons.title: Guard yourself against the love of popularity
lessons.body: A da'i easily feels people accept Islam because of his skill, when Allah is the one who changes hearts, and likes and subscriber counts test sincerity.

glossary.meaning: A house used as a da'wah base in Mecca, and Mus'ab set up a similar one in As'ad's house in Madinah.
One who teaches and recites the Quran; the title of Mus'ab ibn Umair.
An open area near Madinah where As'ad gathered forty people for Friday prayer.
Minority fiqh, referring to Muslims in countries where they are few, including conditions for Friday prayer.
A leader the Prophet appointed to look after his people after the second Aqabah.
The love of popularity; a subtle test for da'is according to Natsir.

dalil.context: The ustaz says this sahih hadith is in Imam Bukhari, and makes it the basis for choosing the two teachers.
dalil.translation: Al-Bara RA said the first to come to us in Madinah were Mus'ab ibn Umair, then Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum, and they taught people to recite the Quran.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this hadith while explaining the trait of a da'i, with the remark that today we can feel its pain through the comments section.
dalil.translation: One who mixes with people and is patient with the hurt of mixing is better than one who does not mix and is not patient with the hurt.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions this hadith in Bukhari and Muslim to show sacrifice whose fruit one does not live to enjoy.
dalil.translation: Khabbab said we migrated with the Prophet ﷺ seeking the face of Allah; some died without enjoying any worldly reward, like Mus'ab ibn Umair, who was killed at Uhud and had no shroud except a single burdah which covered his head but left his feet bare, so the Prophet told us to cover his head with the cloth and his feet with idhkhir grass.

dalil.context: The ustaz says the Prophet accepted that correction without justification and welcomed Abdullah with honour.
dalil.translation: Aisha RA said the verse Abasa was revealed about Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum, who was blind; he came to the Prophet asking to be taught and purified while the Prophet was speaking with Quraysh nobles, and the Prophet frowned and continued his conversation.

dalil.context: Surah Abasa rebuked the Prophet for turning away from Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum, who was blind. The ustaz does not mention the verse number. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
The ustaz says this comes from a tafsir narration, not a hadith with a stated grade.
dalil.translation: Whenever Abdullah ibn Ummi Maktum came, the Prophet ﷺ said welcome to the one because of whom my Lord corrected me.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Mus'ab recited Surah Az-Zukhruf to Usayd and Sa'd, a sirah narration from Al-Bayhaqi that is not in the sahih hadith. Its opening verses are about the Quran in Arabic. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
The ustaz says it is cited in sirah books, and Usayrim accepted Islam on the morning of Uhud then was martyred before he could pray.
dalil.translation: Abu Hurairah asked about a man who entered Paradise without ever praying, then answered that he was Usayrim, Amr ibn Thabit of Banu Abd al-Ashhal; the Prophet ﷺ said he did little but was given a great reward.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions the schools' differences on the minimum number for Friday prayer and the context of minority fiqh.
dalil.translation: Abdul Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik narrated that when Ka'b heard the Friday adhan he prayed mercy for As'ad ibn Zurarah, because he was the first to gather them for Friday prayer at Naqi' al-Khadimat, forty people.

dalil.context: The ustaz mentions Surah Al-Jumu'ah, which later institutionalised Friday prayer with its rules. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Believers! When the call to prayer is made on the day of congregation, hurry towards the reminder of God and leave off your trading––that is better for you, if only you knew––

dalil.context: The ustaz says Prophet Ibrahim already gave us the brand Muslim and we do not need to invent new labels. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: Strive hard for God as is His due: He has chosen you and placed no hardship in your religion, the faith of your forefather Abraham. God has called you Muslims––both in the past and in this [message]––so that the Messenger can bear witness about you and so that you can bear witness about other people. So keep up the prayer, give the prescribed alms, and seek refuge in God: He is your protector––an excellent protector and an excellent helper.

dalil.context: The ustaz says Allah taught a higher moral standard because the Prophet was of a great character. The verse number is not mentioned. (reference identified; verse number not mentioned)
dalil.translation: truly you have a strong character––
